## Blog Implementation Summary

### 1. **Blog Directory Structure**
- **Blog Posts Storage**: `/Users/yogesh/Documents/yogesh/content/blog/`
  - Currently contains 3 markdown files:
    - `agent-harness.md`
    - `manipulating-ai-recommendations.md`
    - `what-6-months-of-building-a-saas-taught-me.md`

- **Blog Components**: `/Users/yogesh/Documents/yogesh/app/components/`
  - `BlogList.js` - Lists all blog posts
  - `BlogSection.js` - Blog section wrapper with theme context
  - `TLDR.js` - TL;DR section component
  - `FloatingNav.js` - Navigation with on-page section links

- **Blog Routes**: `/Users/yogesh/Documents/yogesh/app/[blogId]/`
  - `page.js` - Individual blog post page
  - `opengraph-image.js` - Dynamic OG image generation

### 2. **How Blog Posts Are Stored & Loaded**
**Format**: Markdown files with YAML frontmatter
- **Frontmatter fields**:
  - `title` - Post title
  - `meta_title` - SEO title
  - `social_title` - Title for social sharing (optional, defaults to `title`)
  - `meta_description` - SEO description
  - `published_date` - Publication date (YYYY-MM-DD format)
  - `modified_date` - Last modification date (optional)

**Example from `agent-harness.md`**:
```yaml
---
title: "How to Build an Agent Harness?"
meta_title: "How to Build an Agent Harness?"
social_title: "Building an Agent Harness Is Easier than You Think"
meta_description: "Agent harness is fundamentally an infinite loop of api requests to LLM provider."
published_date: "2026-07-19"
modified_date: "2026-07-19"
---
```

### 3. **Blog Loading & Processing** (`/Users/yogesh/Documents/yogesh/lib/blog.js`)

**Two main functions**:

1. **`getBlogPost(slug)`** - Loads a single blog post
   - Reads markdown file from `content/blog/{slug}.md`
   - Uses `gray-matter` library to extract YAML frontmatter and content
   - Converts markdown to HTML using `marked` library
   - Syntax highlighting via `prismjs` (supports Python, etc.)
   - Builds table of contents from H2+ headings with auto-generated IDs
   - Extracts TL;DR block (special `:::tldr...:::` syntax)
   - Returns: `{ slug, title, meta_title, social_title, meta_description, published_date, modified_date, content, headings, tldrItems }`

2. **`getAllBlogPosts()`** - Lists all blog posts
   - Scans `content/blog/` directory for `.md` files
   - Extracts metadata from each file (without full content rendering)
   - Returns sorted array by `published_date` (newest first)
   - Each post includes: `slug, title, published_date, modified_date, meta_title, social_title, meta_description`

**Special Features**:
- **TLDR Parsing**: Extracts numbered list from `:::tldr\n...\n:::` blocks
- **Heading Navigation**: Generates table of contents with proper heading hierarchy
- **Prism Syntax Highlighting**: Code blocks support language-specific highlighting
- **URL Slug Generation**: Heading IDs created from text (normalized, kebab-case with deduplication)

### 4. **Blog Routing & Page Structure**

**Homepage** (`/Users/yogesh/Documents/yogesh/app/page.js`):
- Displays blog list via `BlogList` component
- Filters out certain posts (e.g., "manipulating-ai-recommendations")
- Uses `getAllBlogPosts()` to fetch posts

**Individual Blog Post** (`/Users/yogesh/Documents/yogesh/app/[blogId]/page.js`):
- **Dynamic route**: `[blogId]` parameter maps to markdown filename
- URL structure: `https://yogesh.co/{slug}` (e.g., `https://yogesh.co/agent-harness`)
- Generates metadata dynamically via `generateMetadata()` async function
- Features:
  - Structured schema.org JSON-LD for SEO
  - Date formatting
  - Rendered HTML content via `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`
  - Conditional TLDR display
  - FloatingNav with on-page section navigation (passed from `headings`)

**OG Image Generation** (`/Users/yogesh/Documents/yogesh/app/[blogId]/opengraph-image.js`):
- Uses Next.js `ImageResponse` (on-the-fly image generation)
- Generates 1200x630px PNG for social sharing
- Displays: "Yogesh" branding, blog title, published date, tagline "Notes on building software"
- Title sizing adjusts based on length (62px or 72px font)

### 5. **Blog-Related Configuration**

**Dependencies** (`package.json`):
- `gray-matter` - YAML frontmatter parsing
- `marked` - Markdown to HTML conversion
- `prismjs` - Syntax highlighting
- `react` & `react-dom` - UI framework
- `tailwindcss` - Styling

**Framework**: Next.js 16.0.10
- App Router (Next.js 13+ directory structure)
- Server-side rendering for blog posts
- Dynamic route generation from markdown files

**Styling** (`globals.css`):
- Custom CSS variables for light/dark themes
- Monokai color scheme for code syntax highlighting
- `.markdown-content` class for blog post styling (1.1rem font, 1.7 line-height)

**SEO Features**:
- Dynamic metadata generation per blog post
- Open Graph image generation
- Twitter card support
- Canonical URLs
- Sitemap generation (`app/sitemap.xml/route.js`) that dynamically includes all blog posts
- JSON-LD structured data for BlogPosting schema

### 6. **Blog Post Display Flow**

1. User visits `/agent-harness` URL
2. Next.js matches to `[blogId]/page.js` with `params.blogId = "agent-harness"`
3. `getBlogPost("agent-harness")` loads `/content/blog/agent-harness.md`
4. Markdown converted to HTML with syntax highlighting
5. Headings extracted for table of contents navigation
6. TL;DR block parsed if present
7. Page rendered with metadata, structured data, and navigation
8. OG image dynamically generated at `/agent-harness/opengraph-image`

This is a **file-based CMS** approach using markdown files as the content source, with no database required. All blog posts are co-located in the `content/blog/` directory for easy management.

   - Returns: `{ slug, title, meta_title, social_title, meta_description, published_date, modified_date, content, headings, tldrItems }`

2. **`getAllBlogPosts()`** - Lists all blog posts
   - Scans `content/blog/` directory for `.md` files
   - Extracts metadata from each file (without full content rendering)
   - Returns sorted array by `published_date` (newest first)
   - Each post includes: `slug, title, published_date, modified_date, meta_title, social_title, meta_description`

**Special Features**:

- URL structure: `https://yogesh.co/{slug}` (e.g., `https://yogesh.co/agent-harness`)
- Generates metadata dynamically via `generateMetadata()` async function
- Features:

  - Conditional TLDR display
  - FloatingNav with on-page section navigation (passed from `headings`)

**OG Image Generation** (`/Users/yogesh/Documents/yogesh/app/[blogId]/opengraph-image.js`):
- Uses Next.js `ImageResponse` (on-the-fly image generation)
- Generates 1200x630px PNG for social sharing

- Title sizing adjusts based on length (62px or 72px font)

### 5. **Blog-Related Configuration**

**Dependencies** (`package.json`):
- `gray-matter` - YAML frontmatter parsing
- `marked` - Markdown to HTML conversion
- `prismjs` - Syntax highlighting

**Framework**: Next.js 16.0.10

- Server-side rendering for blog posts
- Dynamic route generation from markdown files

**Styling** (`globals.css`):
- Custom CSS variables for light/dark themes
- Monokai color scheme for code syntax highlighting
- `.markdown-content` class for blog post styling (1.1rem font, 1.7 line-height)

**SEO Features**:
- Dynamic metadata generation per blog post
- Open Graph image generation
- Twitter card support
- Canonical URLs
- Sitemap generation (`app/sitemap.xml/route.js`) that dynamically includes all blog posts
- JSON-LD structured data for BlogPosting schema

### 6. **Blog Post Display Flow**

1. User visits `/agent-harness` URL
2. Next.js matches to `[blogId]/page.js` with `params.blogId = "agent-harness"`
3. `getBlogPost("agent-harness")` loads `/content/blog/agent-harness.md`
4. Markdown converted to HTML with syntax highlighting
5. Headings extracted for table of contents navigation
6. TL;DR block parsed if present
7. Page rendered with metadata, structured data, and navigation
8. OG image dynamically generated at `/agent-harness/opengraph-image`

This is a **file-based CMS** approach using markdown files as the content source, with no database required. All blog posts are co-located in the `content/blog/` directory for easy management.
